text:
incident-bot: PagerDuty trigger PDL-4823 — routing-policy flapping detected between us-east <-> us-west <-> eu. Auto-escalation: page to #incidents and oncall.
Samir: seeing repeated health-check failures and immediate fallback churn. spikes in 5xx and increased tail latencies.
Oncall: acknowledging, taking lead. paging details?
incident-bot: root cause telemetry: health_probe_timeout increased from 150ms -> 50ms (config drift) on eu probe cluster at 22:14 UTC. Fallback policy 'regional-failover' set to cyclic; probe failures cause sequential fallback hops.
Emily: wait that sounds like the recent probe tuning change from yesterday? Maya pushed a probe config bump on eu to be more aggressive for canaries.
Maya: yep I rolled aggressive probe to catch circuit break early. Didn’t realize fallthrough was cycling through regions. My bad — I was focused on kv-eviction issue.
Samir: ok immediate plan: 1) disable cyclic fallback in routing policy 2) revert probe aggressiveness on eu 3) throttle cross-region health propagation 4) assess customer impact + notify.
Oncall: doing step 1 now — applying policy override to set `routing.policy.failover_mode=static_priority` for service `inference-api` in control-plane.
Oncall: command run:
```
redwoodctl routing set --service inference-api --env prod --policy failover_mode=static_priority --reason "mitigate flap"
```
Oncall: applied. Confirming: policies show static_priority [us-east, us-west, eu] pinned.
Ops-Bot: policy-change event recorded: id=chg-2026031501 user=Oncall scope=inference-api env=prod
Samir: good. now revert probe change on eu cluster. Maya can you revert and restart probes?
Maya: reverting now. patch: `probes/eu/healthy_timeout=150ms` -> deploy started.
Emily: starting quick canary checks against eu probes. Running `curl` healthcheck 50x to confirm flapping stops.
Emily: sample logs show previous pattern:
```
2026-03-15T22:16:02Z healthcheck: timeout=52ms region=eu target=kv-proxy
2026-03-15T22:16:03Z routing: fallback -> us-west (reason: probe_timeout)
2026-03-15T22:16:05Z healthcheck: success region=us-west
2026-03-15T22:16:07Z routing: fallback -> us-east (reason: probe_timeout)
```
Oncall: probe revert finished, restarting probe daemons.
Ops-Bot: probe-deploy event: id=deploy-8746 region=eu user=Maya status=SUCCEEDED
Emily: healthcheck results after revert: 50/50 success, no timeouts. Monitoring for 3 minutes.
Samir: rollbacks looked good. Now we should re-enable a safer failover policy after stabilization. Keep static_priority for next 10m, then switch to priority-with-backoff.
Oncall: set timed policy override for 10m.
Oncall: command run:
```
redwoodctl routing override --service inference-api --duration 10m --policy static_priority
```
Maya: quick note: the original config change included `probemode=aggressive` + `probe_tolerance=2` which made intermittent network blips appear as failures. I'll add a note to the change request to include a canary in multiple regions.
Emily: impact estimate: between 22:14–22:22 UTC ~3.8% of requests experienced elevated error rates (5xx) and ~1.7% latency increase at p95. No enterprise customers reported data loss.
Samir: thanks. paging summary for PD: impact=partial degradation; scope=inference-api global but concentrated in eu; mitigation=reverted probe + static routing override; next actions=monitor 30m, follow-up postmortem, update runbook to forbid aggressive probe changes without cross-region canary and failover-safety flag.
Oncall: handing off to next oncall @Samir in 20m. leaving notes in #oncall-handoffs.
Maya: apologies for the churn — will open a PR with safer defaults and add automated test for fallback loops.
Samir: good. Also check if any model-variant pinning happened during flaps — telemetry shows a few requests hit a fallback variant (`rdx-small-quant-v2`) but that seems incidental, not root cause. We'll include in postmortem.
incident-bot: Incident PDL-4823 -> status: mitigated (policy override + probe revert). Follow-up: postmortem required, severity=P2.
Oncall: creating incident doc and assigning owners: Samir (lead), Maya (probe change), Emily (telemetry + impact). I'll tag infra-eng and eng-releases for rollout checklist.
Emily: quick check — customer-facing note draft: "We experienced transient routing disruptions affecting a subset of inference requests in the EU region. The issue has been mitigated; users may have observed increased errors or latency between 22:14-22:22 UTC. A postmortem will follow." Want me to send?
Samir: yes, schedule for status page update and send to account managers.
Maya: handing off to Samir for long-term follow-up. I'll be available during handoff. :thumbsup:
Oncall: leaving channel, thanks all.
Samir: capturing timeline and action items in incident doc. moving to monitoring for 30m.
incident-bot: thread closed for active mitigation at 22:22 UTC, follow-up tasks created: TASK-1429 (postmortem), TASK-1430 (runbook update), TASK-1431 (automated canary tests).
